discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant. This revealed that ordinary band insulators can be topologically distinct and must host protected, spin-momentum-locked boundary states. Kane, with Fu, extended this to three-dimensional topological insulators and predicted Majorana modes at superconducting interfaces. Molenkamp's group engineered HgTe quantum wells and in 2007 observed quantized edge conduction, the first experimental realisation of the quantum spin Hall state. Together this work created a new organising principle for crystalline solids. Topology is now a basic lens for classifying materials, and it led directly to Weyl semimetals, topological superconductivity and magnetic topological insulators showing the quantum anomalous Hall effect. As with the cuprates, a new class of real materials changed what the community thought was possible.
